message.content:
Let \(A=(1,1,1)\). Since the line through \(A\) intersects the first given line at \(P\), the line lies in the plane containing \(A\) and that first line. Therefore \(Q\) must also lie in this plane.

The first line has point \((1,2,3)\) and direction \((2,3,4)\). A normal vector to the plane containing \(A\) and this line is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{pmatrix}
-
\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\2\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\2\end{pmatrix}
\times
\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\4\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}-2\\4\\-2\end{pmatrix}
\sim
\begin{pmatrix}1\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus the plane through \(A\) has equation
\[
(x-1)-2(y-1)+(z-1)=0
\]
or
\[
x-2y+z=0.
\]

Now \(Q\) lies on the second line:
\[
Q=(-2+s,\;3+2s,\;-1+4s).
\]
Substitute into the plane equation:
\[
(-2+s)-2(3+2s)+(-1+4s)=0.
\]
Simplify:
\[
-2+s-6-4s-1+4s=0
\]
\[
s-9=0
\]
\[
s=9.
\]
Therefore
\[
Q=(-2+9,\;3+18,\;-1+36)=(7,21,35).
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{(7,21,35)}\).
